statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). NQ trades at 29,318.50, down 131.00 points or 0.44%, after breaking the 29,426.75 floor, failing to retrace it, and extending a further 94 points to a fresh session low at 29,315.00, where it now sits about three points above the low. ES is on its own 7,663.50 session low. Tail rises from 17 to 24 on extreme-holding and repeated extension. Stress rises to 74 with the 10-year at 5.027%, VIX up 7.95% to 17.10, WTI at 103.27 and the two-day Federal Reserve meeting opening today.
recommendation: Tail at 24 sits at the top of the watch band, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The seven-point lift from 17 records real new evidence rather than a change of view: the overnight floor that broke last hour was not reclaimed, price extended a further 94 points to a new low, and NQ and ES are simultaneously pinned on their session extremes while the Nikkei reversed from up 0.8% to down 0.32%. Long-end yields at 5.027%, VIX up 7.95% and crude up 1.86% point the same way. What holds the score below the elevated band is magnitude and conflict: the entire Globex range is 180.25 points, or 0.61%, across more than seven hours, Asian semiconductors rebounded this morning with SK Hynix up 1.62% and Samsung up 0.9%, the Nikkei is 221 points off its own low, and Monday's cash session recovered 259.5 points from 28,867.67. Conflicting cross-asset evidence of that kind raises Stress rather than Tail under this framework. Stress at 74 is high and unresolved, but Stress alone does not change the mapped state. The declared danger window from 13:00 to 15:00 UTC covers the US cash open and the first full cash hour, where an unretraced continuation of the overnight break would carry the most weight.
headline: NQ extends the broken floor to a fresh 29,315.00 low and holds three points above it with ES on its own low, the 10-year at 5.027% and VIX up 7.95% as the Fed meeting opens - Tail lifts to 24 with Stress high at 74
body: The development of this hour is the failure of the retracement, not the size of the decline. The 29,426.75 floor that had held since the 22:00 UTC reopen broke last hour and was never reclaimed; instead NQ extended a further 94 points to 29,315.00 and now trades at 29,318.50, down 131.00 points or 0.44%. The Globex range has widened from 86.25 points to 180.25 points, or 0.61%, and the session profile is a sequence of lower lows from the 29,495.25 high with no meaningful recovery of broken levels. ES independently sits on its 7,663.50 low at 7,663.75, down 0.38%, so the two US index futures are aligned rather than one leading the other. That combination - repeated extension after a failed retracement, plus both indices holding at their extremes - is the structure this framework treats as the most reliable precursor of a path that denies mean reversion, and it is why Tail moves from 17 to 24 rather than drifting a point. The cross-asset backdrop points the same direction. The 10-year is at 5.027%, up 3.9 basis points and reported at its highest since 2023, the 30-year is near 5.367% at levels last seen in 2002, the 2-year is 4.69%, WTI is 103.27 up 1.86% and Brent 107.41 up 1.64% with Middle East supply risk unresolved, and VIX is 17.10, up 1.26 or 7.95% from a 15.84 close. A two-day Federal Reserve meeting opens today with more than 90% priced for the first increase since 2023, and Monday's session was driven by a call from Anthropic's chief executive for a slowdown in frontier AI development, backed by other industry leaders, which took the PHLX semiconductor index down almost 6% in its worst day since early July and left the cash Nasdaq-100 at 29,127.16, down 0.82%. The case against a higher score is equally concrete. A 0.61% range over more than seven hours is not directional efficiency in any meaningful sense; it is a slow drift in thin Asian books. Asian semiconductors rebounded this morning rather than extending Monday's decline, with SK Hynix up 1.62%, Samsung up 0.9% and Kioxia up 2.73%, and KOSPI and the mainland indices were positive. The Nikkei, having reversed from up 0.8% to down 0.32%, still trades 221 points above its own session low, which is direct evidence that retracement is functioning in the region even as NQ sits on its extreme. Monday's cash session recovered 259.5 points from its 28,867.67 low. Under the framework used here, conflicting cross-asset evidence of that kind reduces directional conviction and raises Stress; it does not mechanically raise Tail. The honest reading is a genuine and worsening structural signal on a small absolute move, which is why the score sits at the top of the watch band rather than inside the elevated band. The conditional path treats the European cash open at 07:00 UTC as the first liquid test of the break and the US cash open as the decisive one, with the declared danger window at 13:00 to 15:00 UTC. The 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC is a separate rates checkpoint given where the long end trades. No outcome of any of these is observed at the assessment cutoff, and the forecast states them as checkpoints rather than as events that have already resolved.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments are available. Tail entered the window at 20, held a 19 to 23 range through the Asian session and the European handover, peaked at 26 during the European mid-morning chip-led decline and repeated 25 in the following hour, eased through midday, printed 26 again at the US cash open, then decayed steadily through the afternoon and evening to a 14 to 16 plateau across the overnight hours as the opening decline was partly recovered. The final slot at 04:00 UTC lifted to 17 on the first break of the overnight floor. Stress fell from a 79 peak to a 65 to 66 plateau before turning back up to 68 in the closing slot, and Confidence held between 86 and 89 throughout. The window contains three hours in the orange band, all tied to Monday's chip-led decline, and no hour reached the red band.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds 24 through the remainder of the Asian session, then enters the elevated band at 25 for the European cash open at 07:00 UTC and holds 25 across the European mid-morning window that produced Monday's chip-led leg. It eases to 24, 23 and 22 through the European late morning and midday lull, returns to 24 for the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC releases, and peaks at 27 across the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. It eases to 24 and 23 through the US midday, lifts to 25 for the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC, holds 24 and 23 through the post-auction reaction and the power-hour approach, and falls to 21 at the cash close. It drops to 17 inside the futures maintenance halt, recovers to 19 at the Globex reopen, returns to the watch band at 20 across the Tokyo open and the Asian mid-session on Federal Reserve decision day, eases to 19 through the Asian afternoon and the European handover, and closes the horizon at 20 into the European mid-morning ahead of the 12:30 UTC retail sales release and the 18:00 UTC decision. Every forecast value is conditional risk derived from scheduled checkpoints and the currently observed structure, not an assertion that any future price path has already been observed.
